summary: Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak Monasteries and under Sera Khandro, Khenpo Aten, and others. He founded the International Nyingma Society.

Dugald Mackichan (1851–1932) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow, University of Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai (1878–1920) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1888–1890).

Duncan Forbes (1798–1868) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Perth Grammar School and the University of St Andrews. He taught at Calcutta Academy (1823–1826), was Professor of Oriental languages at King's College London (1837–1861), and held a post at the British Museum.

Duncan Ryūken Williams (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Reed College and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD from Boston University in 2001 under Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) studied at Trashichöling, Sera, and Gyuto monasteries under Ngawang Yönten and Tsadru Ngawang Losang. He held professorships at Minzu University of China and Tibet University, and leadership roles at Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and China Tibetology Research Center.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Scottish Church College, Narasinha Dutt College, the University of Calcutta, and Sanskrit College and University.
Durga Prasad Dikshit earned a PhD from the University of Lucknow, studying under Baij Nath Puri, R. K. Dikshit, and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi. He worked in Indology and history/archaeology.
Dušan Zbavitel (1925–2012) was an Indology scholar who studied at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný from 1945 to 1949 and later held a post there.
Dwarikadas Shastri (born 1922) studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in Indology and Buddhist studies. He founded Bauddha Bharati and served as co-editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dwight Whitney Learned (1848–1943) worked in religious studies and Japanology. After studying at Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he taught at Thayer College (1872–1875) and served as Professor of Church History and Biblical Theology at Doshisha University (1875–1928).
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Presidency University, Patna University, and the University of Calcutta.

Dylan Esler works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, holding degrees from SOAS University of London and KU Leuven. He has held posts at KU Leuven, Ruhr University Bochum, and 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, having studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen. He founded Mangala Shri Bhuti and was a Buddhist philosophy professor at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He founded Nitartha International, Nitartha Institute, and Nalandabodhi, and directed the Nitartha and Kamalashila Institutes.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, educated at Sakya College and SOAS under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others. He founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.
Dániel Balogh is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology who has held posts at the British Museum and Eötvös Loránd University.
Dávid Jónás is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Tibetology who completed a PhD in 2019 and became an assistant lecturer in 2021 at Eötvös Loránd University.
